title: Text Embeddings: Vectorizing Text
why: “Something light, without meat” — sending the whole menu is expensive, and LIKE won't find the lobio, because those words aren't in its description. Today we learn about embeddings: turning text into a vector where a similar meaning is close together. This is the foundation of semantic search, RAG and agent memory — the whole second half of the module stands on it.
outcomes: You'll explain what an embedding and a vector are, why a similar meaning is “close”, and why vectors from different models can't be compared
You'll register an `IEmbeddingGenerator` (`gemini-embedding-2`, 768 dimensions) and get vectors with `GenerateVectorAsync` / `GenerateAsync`
You'll write the question and the document with the right task prefix and explain why the search is asymmetric
You'll calculate cosine similarity (by hand and with `TensorPrimitives`) and write a semantic search for the menu with a top 3

review.q: Why doesn't LIKE find the lobio for “without meat”, and what does an embedding do differently?
review.a: LIKE looks for words, and those words aren't in the description · an embedding turns the text into a vector where a similar meaning is close — regardless of language and words

review.q: How is an embedding model different from a chat model? Which one do we use and at what size?
review.a: It doesn't write text — it returns one vector, and only the input is charged · `IEmbeddingGenerator` · `gemini-embedding-2`, 768 dimensions

review.q: Why can't we “just” change the model if vectors are already stored?
review.a: Every model (and size) has its own “map” — vectors from different models can't be compared · changing the model = calculating every vector again

review.q: What is a task prefix, and why do the question and the document have different ones?
review.a: Asymmetric search: a short “wish” ↔ long “facts” · `task: search result | query: …` and `title: … | text: …` · always by the same rule

review.q: What does cosine similarity measure, and how do we read the number?
review.a: The angle between two vectors: 1 — the same direction, 0 — nothing in common · the number depends on the model — we compare and sort, we don't judge it on its own

quiz.explain: A word and a meaning are different — that's what we need an embedding for.

quiz.explain: A vector is a point in space; points with a similar meaning stand close together.

quiz.explain: An embedding model reflects the meaning, and the language much less.

quiz.q: We stored vectors with `gemini-embedding-2`. Now we're moving to another embedding model. What do we have to do?
options: The old vectors can't be compared with the new ones — all of them have to be calculated again

quiz.q: Why do we take 768 dimensions instead of 3072?
options: It's a recommended size: good quality, a 4 times smaller vector — less space and a faster search
quiz.explain: Google recommends 768, 1536 and 3072; 768 is enough for our task.

quiz.q: What type is the result of `GenerateVectorAsync`?
quiz.explain: An embedding is a list of floats; on many texts GenerateAsync returns GeneratedEmbeddings.

quiz.q: Why is the question written with `task: search result | query: …` and the document with `title: … | text: …`?
options: The search is asymmetric: a short question and a long document; the prefix tells the model the role and raises the quality
quiz.explain: The rule is the same everywhere: every document in one format, every question in the other.

options: The vectors point in the same direction — very similar
quiz.explain: 1 — the same direction, 0 — perpendicular (nothing in common).

quiz.q: Two scores: 0.71 and 0.38. The right conclusion:
options: The first pair is more similar; we compare the numbers, we don't judge them on their own — the absolute value depends on the model
quiz.explain: In a search, the ordering is what matters.

quiz.q: We calculate the menu's vectors once (`/menu/index`), and on a question only the question's vector. Why?
options: The menu rarely changes; 200 dishes' vectors on every question = money and time
A question's vector can't be stored
Gemini takes one request per minute
quiz.explain: We calculate once and store; in lecture 10 — in the database.

summary: **Embedding**: text → vector (a list of numbers), where **a similar meaning is close together** — regardless of language and words.
The vector is generated by a **separate embedding model**: `gemini-embedding-2`, **768** dimensions. One model = one “map”.
**Task prefix**: the question — `task: search result | query: …`, the document — `title: … | text: …`; always by the same rule.

**Cosine similarity** — the angle between two vectors (1 — similar, 0 — nothing in common); `TensorPrimitives.CosineSimilarity`. Search: the menu once → vectors; a question → cosine with everything → top 3.
